questions.question_text: Form the partial differential equation by eliminating $f$ from $f(x^2+y^2+z^2,x+y+z)=0$.
questions.answer: The gradients of the two arguments are dependent: $(x+zp)(1+q)-(y+zq)(1+p)=0$, which simplifies to $(y-z)p+(z-x)q=x-y$.

questions.question_text: Write the boundary conditions of an infinite long plate bounded by 2 parallel edges and an end at right angles to them. The breadth is $\pi$. This end is maintained at a constant temperature $u_0$ at all points and the other edges at zero temperature.

questions.question_text: If $F[f(x)]=F(s)$, then prove that $F[f(x)\cos ax]=\frac12[F(s-a)+F(s+a)]$.
questions.answer: Write $\cos ax=(e^{iax}+e^{-iax})/2$, apply the modulation shift theorem, and use linearity.

questions.question_text: Solve $p^2+q^2=x+y$.
questions.answer: Separation gives $p^2-x=a$ and $q^2-y=-a$. Integrating gives $z=\frac23(x+a)^{3/2}+\frac23(y-a)^{3/2}+b$, with independent sign branches where real.

questions.question_text: If the half-range Fourier cosine series of $f(x)=x$ in $0<x<l$ is $f(x)=\frac l2-\frac{4l}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{\cos((2n-1)\pi x/l)}{(2n-1)^2}$, deduce the value of $1/1^4+1/3^4+1/5^4+\cdots$.
questions.answer: Parseval gives $l^2/3=l^2/4+\frac12(16l^2/\pi^4)\sum_{n\ge1}(2n-1)^{-4}$. Therefore the sum is $\pi^4/96$.

questions.question_text: Solve (i) $z=p^2+q^2$ (ii) $z=px+qy+p^2-q^2$.
questions.answer: (i) A complete integral is $z=[(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2]/4$; differentiating verifies the PDE. (ii) The Clairaut complete integral is $z=ax+by+a^2-b^2$; its envelope is $z=(y^2-x^2)/4$.

questions.question_text: (i) Find the general solution of $x(z^2-y^2)p+y(x^2-z^2)q=z(y^2-x^2)$. (ii) Solve $(D^2-2DD\prime)z=x^3y+e^{2x}$.
questions.answer: (i) The characteristic invariants are $xyz$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2$, hence $\Phi(xyz,x^2+y^2+z^2)=0$. (ii) $z=\phi(y)+\psi(y+2x)+e^{2x}/4+x^5y/20+x^6/60$.

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier series of $f(x)=x+x^2$ in $(-\pi,\pi)$. Hence deduce $\sum 1/n^2=\pi^2/6$.
questions.answer: $x+x^2=\pi^2/3+\sum_{n\ge1}[4(-1)^n\cos nx/n^2+2(-1)^{n+1}\sin nx/n]$. At $x=\pi$ the periodic endpoint mean is $\pi^2$, giving $\sum1/n^2=\pi^2/6$.
Discrete harmonic analysis gives $a_0/2=2425/12$, $a_1=107/2+371\sqrt3/12$, $b_1=727/12+35\sqrt3$, $a_2=-155/12$, $b_2=21\sqrt3/4$. Thus $y\approx a_0/2+a_1\cos x+b_1\sin x+a_2\cos2x+b_2\sin2x$.

questions.question_text: A tightly stretched string with fixed end points $x=0$ and $x=l$ is initially in a position given by $y(x,0)=y_0\sin^3(\pi x/l)$. If it is released from rest from this position, find the displacement $y$ at any time and at any distance from the end $x=0$.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^3\theta=(3\sin\theta-\sin3\theta)/4$ and wave speed $c$, $y=\frac{y_0}{4}[3\sin(\pi x/l)\cos(\pi ct/l)-\sin(3\pi x/l)\cos(3\pi ct/l)]$.

questions.question_text: A rod, 30 cms long has its ends A and B kept at 20°C and 80°C respectively, until steady state conditions prevail. The temperature at each end is then suddenly reduced to 0°C and kept so. Find the resulting temperature function $u(x,t)$, taking $x=0$ at A.
questions.answer: The initial profile is $20+2x$. Its sine coefficients on $(0,30)$ are $b_n=\frac{2}{n\pi}[20-80(-1)^n]$. For diffusivity $\alpha^2$, $u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n\sin(n\pi x/30)e^{-\alpha^2n^2\pi^2t/900}$.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Applications of Partial Differential Equations

questions.question_text: A rectangular plate with insulated surface is 10 cm wide and so long compared to its width that it may be considered infinite length without introducing appreciable error. If the temperature at short edge $y=0$ is $u=20x$ for $0\le x\le5$, $u=20(10-x)$ for $5\le x\le10$ and all the other three edges are kept at 0°C, find the steady state temperature at any point of the plate.
questions.answer: The boundary sine coefficients are $b_n=800\sin(n\pi/2)/(n^2\pi^2)$. The decaying harmonic solution is $u(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_ne^{-n\pi y/10}\sin(n\pi x/10)$.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Applications of Partial Differential Equations

questions.question_text: The bounding radii $\theta=0$ and $\theta=\pi/2$ of a circular quadrant are kept at 0°C and the temperature along the curve is kept at $50(\pi\theta-2\theta^2)$°C. Find the temperature distribution at any point of the plate and also at $(a/2,\pi/4)$ if the radius is $a$.
questions.answer: Separation gives $u(r,\theta)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{100[1-(-1)^n]}{\pi n^3}(r/a)^{2n}\sin(2n\theta)$. At $(a/2,\pi/4)$ this is $\frac{200}{\pi}\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{(-1)^k}{4^{2k+1}(2k+1)^3}$.
questions.chapter: Unit 3: Applications of Partial Differential Equations

questions.question_text: Find the Fourier transform of $f(x)=1-|x|$ if $|x|<1$, $f(x)=0$ if $|x|>1$, and hence find $\int_0^\infty\sin^4t/t^4\,dt$ using Parseval’s identity.
questions.answer: The unnormalized transform is $F(s)=4\sin^2(s/2)/s^2$. Parseval gives $\int_{-1}^1(1-|x|)^2dx=2/3=(1/\pi)\int_0^\infty F(s)^2ds$. Substitution $s=2t$ yields $\int_0^\infty\sin^4t/t^4\,dt=\pi/3$.

questions.question_text: (i) Evaluate $\int_0^\infty x^2dx/[(x^2+a^2)(x^2+b^2)]$ using transform methods. (ii) Find Fourier cosine transform of $e^{-a^2x^2}$ and hence evaluate Fourier sine transform of $xe^{-a^2x^2}$.
questions.answer: (i) For $a,b>0$, Parseval for the sine transforms of $e^{-ax}$ and $e^{-bx}$ gives $\pi/[2(a+b)]$. (ii) For $a>0$, $F_c=e^{-s^2/(4a^2)}/(\sqrt2a)$. Differentiating, $F_s[xe^{-a^2x^2}]=-F_c\prime(s)=s e^{-s^2/(4a^2)}/(2\sqrt2a^3)$.
